text:
sara: Quick debrief from today's cross-card max-batch sweep (A10/T4/L4/A100/H100). Posted raw profiles and a short summary — we need to land softcaps and a per-card token budget policy before next canary.

mike: Nice writeup. TL;DR numbers? Which cards are hitting kernel fallback due to KV frag? :eyes:

sara: TL;DR: H100 and A100 show best packed throughput with higher max_tokens, but H100 KV frag causes ~6-8% tail latency spikes at high batch tokens. L4 and T4 are very sensitive to mixed-length packing; lowering max_batch_tokens reduces throughput less than it reduces tail. A10 sits in middle.

mike: Can you paste the head/raw numbers from the sweep (p50/p99 throughput and p99 latency) for each card? A single table would help.

sara: pasted below. these are steady-state numbers from 30m runs, production-like mix (30% short, 50% med, 20% long).

```
card, max_tokens_per_batch, max_batch, p50_tokens/s, p99_latency_ms
A10, 48k, 48, 12000, 180
T4, 16k, 24, 6000, 260
L4, 10k, 16, 5200, 300
A100, 64k, 72, 22000, 120
H100, 96k, 96, 30000, 160 (with 6-8% spikes)
```

jeff: Important note from kernel selection side: H100 kernels (v2) degrade when KV cache fragmentation >25%. We saw fragmentation happen when mixed long/short sequences are packed aggressively — continuous batching heuristic currently doesn't preempt fragmenting buckets.

olga: Hmm, fragmentation flagged on H100 — is that KV cache eviction because of in-place packing? Can we bias queue policy to prefer homogeneous-length slices for H100?

jeff: Yes. Two quick levers: 1) enforce a stricter max_tokens_per_batch for any slice that would push KV share >25% for that cardclass, 2) add a short-window affinity when forming slices so we group similar seq len (cheap approximate: bucket by len
<128, 128-1024, >1024).

build-bot: profiling artifact uploaded: https://artifacts.redwood/prof/2869999001/kv-frag-h100-0308.tar.gz :white_check_mark:

mike: Proposed policy (softcaps, not hard):
```
policy_v0 = {
  "A10": ["max_tokens": "48k", "max_batch": "48", "softcap_pct": "90%"],
  "T4": ["max_tokens": "16k", "max_batch": "24", "softcap_pct": "85%"],
  "L4": ["max_tokens": "10k", "max_batch": "16", "softcap_pct": "80%"],
  "A100": ["max_tokens": "64k", "max_batch": "72", "softcap_pct": "92%"],
  "H100": ["max_tokens": "80k", "max_batch": "88", "softcap_pct": "88%", "kv_frag_threshold": "25%"]
}
```

olga: +1 but tweak L4 to prefer `quantized_kernel` fallback at >70% token usage to avoid p99 jumps. Also add realtime alert: if kv_frag > 20% for H100 for 3 consecutive mins, reduce H100 max_tokens_per_batch by 15%.

jeff: We should also change the continuous-batching heuristic to consider kernel fit score (a cached heuristic) when deciding to merge slices. Current merge heuristic is length-first; add kernel-fit multiplier so we avoid merges that force worse kernel. Example pseudo: `score = len_score * kernel_fit_factor * age_bonus`

sara: Action items: @mike implement policy_v0 as softcaps in config and schedule a canary tomorrow AM; @jeff add kernel-fit multiplier and a short-window bucket affinity; @olga add the H100 kv_frag alert and quant-kernel fallback rule; I will run 2 canaries (prod-1 small traffic, prod-2 staged) and collect 1h traces.

mike: On it. I'll push a config canary and add per-route telemetry to catch regressions quickly.

jeff: Also logging proposal: annotate batching decision with `kernel_choice_reason` and `kv_proj_estimate` so postmortems can point to the heuristic that picked the merge. Minimal overhead.

sara: Agree, add those tags.

olga: If everyone is good, can we freeze the H100 hardcap change until the canary results? prefer softcap first. :thumbsup:

mike: softcap + canary + alerting = plan.

sara: cool — I'll file the follow-ups in the runbook and link results in this thread after canary. Thanks all.
